title: Workflow action pin checker misses flow-sequence uses
description: The commit adds `ci/checks/security/check-workflow-action-pins.py` and wires it into the workflow and lint paths as the enforcement mechanism for immutable GitHub Actions pins. The parser checks normal block mappings and explicit flow mappings delimited with `{ ... }`, but it does not detect YAML's valid implicit mapping entries inside flow sequences. A workflow line like `steps: [ uses: actions/checkout@v7 ]` parses as a step containing `uses: actions/checkout@v7`, but `validate_workflow_directory()` returns no errors because `flow_mapping_uses_values()` only attempts extraction after `{` or commas while already inside a braced flow mapping. Since balanced `[...]` flow syntax is accepted rather than rejected, a PR can hide mutable external actions from the newly introduced full-SHA pin check.

title: Git status provenance check can execute repo fsmonitor hooks
description: The commit introduces `git_worktree_clean()`, which calls `git -C <root> status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all` on the connector and framework roots. `git status` is not a passive metadata read: it can invoke a repository-configured fsmonitor hook via `core.fsmonitor`. If `CONNECTOR_ROOT` points at a malicious local checkout containing a `.git/config` with `core.fsmonitor` set to an attacker-controlled executable, running the no-CRS evidence `init` path or `validate --check status|completeness|all` will execute that command as the CI/developer user. The previous provenance lookup used `rev-parse`, which does not invoke this hook in the same way; the new `status` call introduces the execution path. This can be mitigated by avoiding `git status` on untrusted repositories or invoking Git with safe overrides such as `-c core.fsmonitor=false` and other config/hook-disabling controls.

title: APXS auto-discovery trusts shared /var/tmp cache
description: The new framework_find_apxs() fallback searches CONNECTOR_COMPONENT_CACHE and BUILD_ROOT for executable apxs/apxs2 files. On local runs where RUNNER_TEMP/TMPDIR are not set, these roots default to /var/tmp/ModSecurity-conector-verified, a predictable shared location. The code only checks that the candidate is executable; it does not verify that the directory was created by the current user/run, has safe ownership/permissions, or is under a private per-run directory. A local attacker on the same host can create /var/tmp/ModSecurity-conector-verified/component-cache/builds/connectors/apache/<name>/httpd/bin/apxs before the victim runs connector checks. The modified find_apxs_or_blocked() will then return that attacker-controlled executable. Existing helper code such as ci_resolve_apache_from_apxs() executes the returned APXS path to query configuration, and connector/build scripts commonly execute APXS during Apache module builds, giving command execution as the victim running the framework.

title: Shared /tmp auto-discovery enables smoke cache poisoning
description: The new connector_smoke_default_verified_roots function always adds /tmp/ModSecurity-conector-verified and /var/tmp/ModSecurity-conector-verified search locations, even when those paths were not configured for the current run. find_runtime_binary now searches these shared locations for executable connector runtimes, and connector_smoke_resolve_modsecurity_backend now scans their component-cache directories for libmodsecurity manifests/prefixes. Because /tmp and /var/tmp are shared writable locations on many developer and CI hosts, another local user or a previous untrusted job can pre-create a matching tree such as /tmp/ModSecurity-conector-verified/bin/envoy or /tmp/ModSecurity-conector-verified/component-cache/builds/modsecurity/*/manifest.json with attacker-controlled headers and libmodsecurity.so. A later smoke run can then select and execute/load that artifact without checksum, ownership, or provenance verification. Before this commit, discovery was limited to configured cache/build roots; the new hard-coded shared fallbacks introduce the poisoning path.

title: Lighttpd build trusts staged source and unsafe build paths
description: The new lighttpd build support treats any existing LIGHTTPD_SOURCE_STAGE_DIR as trusted and skips the pinned download and SHA256 verification path. With ALLOW_RUNTIME_BUILDS=1, the script then runs that directory's configure script. The staged source directory is not required to be under the component cache and is not tied to a verified archive, so a poisoned cache or attacker-controlled environment can cause arbitrary code execution in the CI/build account. Separately, LIGHTTPD_BUILD_ROOT is environment-controlled and is deleted with rm -rf. The only under-cache check used for it is a raw string prefix check, so values containing ../ can pass as if they are under CONNECTOR_COMPONENT_CACHE while resolving outside it. This bypasses the intended path restrictions and can delete or recreate directories outside the generated component cache.

title: RESPONSE_BODY report guard now promotes pass-through to PASS
description: RESPONSE_BODY pass-through cases explicitly do not prove that a connector can inspect and block response bodies. Before this commit, those rows were rendered as RESPONSE_BODY_PASS_THROUGH or prefixed non-promoted statuses, and check-response-body-promotion.py rejected any RESPONSE_BODY row that appeared as plain PASS. The commit sets RESPONSE_BODY_PASS_THROUGH_STATUS to PASS, makes response_body_pass_through_status() ignore classification, collapses all pass/fail classifications to plain PASS/FAIL, and removes the plain-PASS checks from the promotion guard. update-runtime-snapshot.py then serializes this computed value as matrix_status. As a result, a normal passing response_body_pass pass-through run, or a malicious connector/runtime summary reporting a RESPONSE_BODY-related case as pass, can be published in runtime matrices as plain PASS even though promotion_allowed remains false and the YAML limitations say pass-through is not blocking proof. This undermines the framework's security-evidence integrity and can create false assurance that a WAF connector supports RESPONSE_BODY enforcement.

title: PR-controlled OSV workflow can forge security evidence
description: The pull_request job in ci-security-osv.yml explicitly checks out github.event.pull_request.head.sha, then installs requirements-ci.lock from that checkout, runs ci/tools/fetch-security-tool.py and ci/tooling/security-tools.lock.yml from that same untrusted checkout, and finally runs ci/checks/security/check-json-result.py and compare-osv-results.py from the PR. Because these are the controls that are supposed to validate and compare the OSV results, a malicious PR can modify them to fetch a benign/fake scanner, always return clean JSON, mark evidence_valid=true, and cause the workflow to upload apparently valid OSV comparison artifacts. The workflow has read-only repository permissions, so this is not a token-exfiltration or write-token RCE issue, but it undermines the integrity of the newly introduced dependency-security evidence and required check result.

title: Workflow checker misses serialized secret contexts
description: The commit introduces ci/checks/security/check-github-actions-workflows.py to enforce the repository's workflow trust boundary. Its secret and github.token detection only matches direct property/index access, such as secrets.FOO, secrets['FOO'], github.token, or github['token']. GitHub Actions expressions can also expose entire contexts, for example ${{ toJSON(secrets) }} or ${{ toJSON(github) }}. Those strings do not match the new regexes, so contains_secret_reference() and contains_github_token_reference() return false. As a result, an unsafe pull_request workflow could place all available secrets into an environment variable, or a workflow/job-level environment could expose the github context including github.token under another name, while the new checker reports success. The currently committed workflows do not contain such a bypass, but the newly introduced security gate has a false negative that can provide false assurance for future workflow changes.

title: Connector report normalization can overwrite symlink targets
description: Before this commit, normalize_localized_overview_report_links returned unless OUTPUT_ROOT was the framework root. The commit removed that guard, so when generate-case-matrix.py is run against an untrusted connector repository, it now opens CONNECTOR_ROOT/reports/testing/test-coverage-overview.de.md directly. Path.is_file() follows symlinks, and write_text() follows the same symlink. A malicious connector repository can therefore add reports/testing/test-coverage-overview.de.md as a symlink to a writable file outside the connector tree; if the target contains a legacy generated-report link or a local path token that portable_markdown_text changes, the generator will overwrite the symlink target. This bypasses the ReportLayout._write_known allowed-output check used for normal generated reports and weakens the report-output confinement described by the project threat model.

title: Protocol evidence accepts payload-capturing curl commands
description: The commit adds protocol-client evidence validation intended to prove that forced H2/H3 probes are payload-free. However, _validate_command() only checks that the command text contains the substring "--output /dev/null" and uses a regex that only rejects forbidden flags when they are followed by whitespace or end-of-line. A crafted command can therefore include a valid safe-looking output option and then a later overriding option such as "--output /tmp/leaked-body", or use equals-form capture options such as "--dump-header=/tmp/headers" or "--trace-ascii=/tmp/trace". Curl accepts these forms, but the validator does not reject them. Because no_crs_baseline.py copies externally supplied protocol-client artifact bundles into the canonical run and then delegates validation to this checker, a malicious or compromised connector/harness can provide artifacts that pass as managed payload-free evidence while the recorded command would have captured response payloads or headers. This undermines the privacy and integrity guarantees of the new evidence path and can support false protocol PASS claims.

title: Unvalidated engine-version artifact can leak secrets
description: The commit adds full-lifecycle engine sidecar copying. For engine_version, the only content validation is that the source text is non-empty; unlike the digest artifacts, it has no bounded schema, length limit, character allowlist, or forbidden-payload/secret check. The file is then copied verbatim to run_dir/engine-version.txt and added to the manifest. The canonical body-payload/privacy validator scans JSON/JSONL artifacts and .log files under logs/, but not root-level .txt artifacts, so a malicious connector/finalize invocation can place sensitive content such as CI environment data, Authorization headers, or body sentinels into engine-version.txt while validate --check all still succeeds. This undermines the framework's canonical evidence privacy guarantees and can leak secrets if run artifacts are uploaded from CI.

title: apxs discovery executes untrusted cache candidates
description: The new framework_apxs_has_usable_headers helper runs every discovered apxs candidate with `-q INCLUDEDIR` to decide whether it has headers. framework_find_apxs applies this helper to APXS_BIN/APXS, PATH candidates, and globbed entries under CONNECTOR_COMPONENT_CACHE and BUILD_ROOT. As a result, a malicious executable named `apxs` placed in a searched cache/build location is executed during discovery, even if it is stale, incomplete, and ultimately not selected. This expands a lookup function that previously only resolved executable paths into a code-execution sink for cache/build-root contents. In environments that reuse component caches across trust boundaries or allow untrusted connector/build artifacts to populate these paths, this can turn cache poisoning into CI/local code execution under the smoke runner user.

title: Phase-4 evidence bypasses integration-mode binding
description: For full_lifecycle artifacts, events are supposed to be bound to the selected manifest/result integration_mode. event_for_case() only prefers matching-mode events; if none match, it deliberately keeps the wrong-mode candidates so callers can report a mismatch. However, normalize_case_record() does not apply the new canonical_event_errors(..., integration_mode=...) failures to Phase-4 PASS records. Phase-4 validation calls phase4_pass_errors(), which still validates only the connector and never receives the selected integration_mode. As a result, a Phase-4 record can remain PASS using a raw event whose integration_mode differs from the selected full-lifecycle host profile. This can let compatibility-path or stale events satisfy selected native full-lifecycle Phase-4 evidence and create misleading PASS results in generated evidence artifacts. The completeness validator later added in this commit can detect the mismatch, but finalize_run() can still write the PASS record before such validation is run.

title: HAProxy shared cache can be forged to reuse attacker binary
description: The new HAProxy managed-cache path accepts HAPROXY_BIN outside BUILD_ROOT when it appears under CONNECTOR_COMPONENT_CACHE/builds/connectors/haproxy/<64-hex>/... and has matching cache marker JSON. However, the marker and manifest checks are only self-consistency checks over attacker-writable files in the same cache root: the cache key is a plain SHA-256 of attacker-chosen identity data, not a signature or trusted digest of the HAProxy binary. The later provenance check only verifies that haproxy.provenance contains expected text lines for version/source/SHA, which an attacker who can write the cache can also forge. If a CI or developer workflow reuses this shared component cache across trust boundaries, a malicious earlier job can plant a fake complete cache entry and executable; a later trusted prepare step will skip rebuilding and report the forged HAPROXY_BIN as ready, leading downstream smoke runs to execute the attacker-controlled binary.

title: Synthetic probe can mint real-host lifecycle evidence
description: The commit adds synchronized_upstream.py to generate first-byte lifecycle evidence. The CLI only blocks real_host evidence when --target-port is omitted. If a caller sets a fixed --listen-port and passes the same port as --target-port with --evidence-origin real_host, the helper connects directly to its own synthetic upstream, yet run_client_barrier copies the caller-provided origin into the evidence and sets promotion_eligible=true. Downstream promotion gates trust evidence_origin == real_host, so a malicious or compromised connector harness can create promotion-eligible first-byte/no-full-buffer evidence without exercising a real connector path, then pair it with crafted events/case records to pass the new lifecycle checks and overstate connector security coverage.

title: Phase-4 content-type cases can falsely PASS on wrong status
description: The commit adds `phase4_out_of_scope_content_type` and `phase4_missing_content_type` with `expected_status` set to 200. These cases are treated as Phase-4 semantic cases, so `normalize_case_record()` bypasses the generic `expected_status` comparison and delegates to `phase4_pass_errors()`. The new content-type branches only require that the host-observed `actual_status` equals the event's `visible_http_status`; they do not require either value to equal the catalog's expected 200. As a result, a host/connector evidence file can mark these cases PASS with an observable wrong status such as 500, as long as the event also reports visible status 500. This weakens the evidence contract and can make generated no-CRS reports falsely claim support for content-type scope behavior.

title: Phase-4 log-only evidence marks RESPONSE_BODY verified
description: The new Phase-4 model separates a narrow `phase4_rule_observed` case from actual disruptive outcomes, but the aggregate result now treats `phase4_rule_observed` as `response_body_verified`. `phase4_rule_observed` returns PASS after only the canonical Phase-4 event/rule checks and does not require a client-visible block, pre-commit deny, connection abort, or expected HTTP status. The helper also derives `phase4_rule_observed` from `phase4_deny_after_commit_log_only`, whose intended outcome is pass-through/log-only after headers were committed. As a result, a connector that only observes/logs a RESPONSE_BODY rule can set `response_body_verified=true`, and the validator recomputes the same incorrect predicate, so validation will not catch the false claim. This undermines report integrity and may create false assurance that RESPONSE_BODY enforcement is verified.

title: Collector case-list results can mask failed source status
description: The new source_records() branch accepts collector payloads with "cases" as a list. finalize_run() then records the top-level source status using str(...).upper() and computes source_failure with an exact membership test for "FAIL". Known aliases such as "failed" and "error" are accepted for per-case statuses elsewhere via STATUS_ALIASES, but are not applied to the top-level source status. As a result, a source result like {"status":"failed", "cases":[...PASS case records...]} is now accepted; source_statuses becomes ["FAILED"], source_failure is false, and if the listed cases satisfy the pass gates the canonical result can be PASS. The newly added status validation repeats the same exact "FAIL" check, so it does not catch the inconsistency. This can undermine report integrity for CI evidence generated from connector-owned or collector-produced JSON.

title: No-CRS summary trusts forged PASS result files
description: The introduced summarize path loads each connector's result.json with find_result() and then directly uses the unvalidated status, evidence_stages, capabilities_verified, group_statuses, and status_counts fields to generate JSON and Markdown reports. It does not call validate_run() or require manifest.json, inventory/run.json, results.jsonl, events.jsonl, checksums, PASS gates, or capability consistency before rendering PASS. The Makefile no-crs-summary target invokes this summarizer directly and does not depend on check-no-crs-evidence. As a result, an attacker who can place or alter files under the evidence root, such as a malicious connector harness/repository in CI, can create minimal forged result.json files claiming PASS and have the canonical all-connector report show connector or even overall PASS despite no runtime evidence.

title: Runtime provisioning helpers bypass download/build opt-in
description: The prepare-* runtime scripts intentionally require ALLOW_RUNTIME_DOWNLOADS=1, and lighttpd additionally requires ALLOW_RUNTIME_BUILDS=1, before fetching artifacts or executing a source build. The new require_or_provision_envoy, require_or_provision_traefik, and require_or_provision_lighttpd functions call those prepare scripts with these variables set internally. As a result, a caller that only asks to require/provision a runtime can trigger network downloads, and in the lighttpd case execution of configure/make from downloaded source, without the operator or CI job explicitly opting in. This weakens the supply-chain guardrail described by the existing prepare scripts and can unexpectedly execute external runtime provisioning code in CI or developer environments.

title: Runtime path guard now allows source checkout writes
description: The new ci_path_is_configured_project_path helper is used as an early success condition in assert_not_system_path_for_write and assert_safe_runtime_path. This means any path under REPO_ROOT, CONNECTOR_ROOT, or FRAMEWORK_ROOT is treated as safe and returns before the existing checks that block writes inside read-only/source checkouts. The commit also allows /src/* unconditionally. Build and smoke scripts rely on assert_safe_runtime_path before creating build/log/output directories and before safe_remove_runtime_path performs rm -rf during REFRESH flows. As a result, an attacker or unsafe CI configuration that can influence BUILD_ROOT, NGINX_BUILD_DIR, APACHE_BUILD_ROOT, LOG_DIR, or related variables can cause generated artifacts to be written into the source checkout, or can remove checkout subdirectories with REFRESH=1. The previous version rejected these source-checkout paths.

title: Unescaped run IDs allow generated Markdown report injection
description: The new report-governance metadata treats the connector repository as an input source for verified_run_id: it reads VERIFIED_RUN_ID from the environment or verified_run_id/run_id/snapshot_date/commit from reports/testing/runtime-validation-snapshot.json under the connector root. Those values are then interpolated directly into generated Markdown blockquote headers and data-source tables inside backtick-delimited spans. Because only strip() is applied, an attacker controlling a connector repository or generated runtime snapshot can include backticks, pipes, or embedded newlines to break out of the code span/table and inject arbitrary Markdown or HTML into generated reports. If those reports are published in a trusted portal or less-restrictive Markdown renderer, this can spoof security evidence or become stored HTML/Markdown injection.

title: Missing HAPROXY_BIN flag enables unsafe binary fallback
description: Before this commit, a non-empty runtime binary variable such as HAPROXY_BIN was treated as authoritative: if the configured path did not exist or was not executable, resolution failed closed. The new find_runtime_binary logic only treats a non-empty value as authoritative when connector_smoke_runtime_env_was_set reports a matching ${VAR}_WAS_SET flag. The commit added flags only for ENVOY_BIN, TRAEFIK_BIN, and LIGHTTPD_BIN, but HAPROXY_BIN remains a defaulted non-empty variable from common.sh. As a result, when the expected HAPROXY_BIN path is absent, require_local_binary HAPROXY_BIN haproxy now searches broad runtime roots and returns the first executable named haproxy. In a CI or shared build-root setting, a stale or attacker-placed executable can therefore be selected and later run by a connector harness instead of failing with BLOCKED evidence.

title: Phase-1 gap test can be falsely promoted as PASS
description: The patched YAML no longer tries to deny on REQUEST_BODY in phase 1. Instead, phase 1 is only a pass/nolog SecAction, and the actual blocking assertion is moved to a phase-2 SecRule. The expected rule_id is also the phase-2 rule. Because the test still declares phase1 capability and remains in the phase1 case path, a connector that never enforces the phase-1 marker can still pass by blocking in phase 2. The changed limitation text also removes the explicit connector-gap / non-promoted wording. In the reporting path, cases without an explicit non-active metadata classification default to active, and active PASS observations are promotion eligible. The former_xfail flag limits default smoke discovery, but explicit/force-all runtime evidence can still be represented as promotion eligible, creating false assurance about phase-1 request-body handling.

title: RUN_ONE_CASE bypasses connector smoke evidence checks
description: ci/connector-smoke-common.sh now exits with status 0 when the harness returns 0, RUN_ONE_CASE=1, and a non-empty result.json exists. This happens before the existing guard that requires $RESULTS_DIR/<connector>-results.jsonl to be present. The new check does not parse result.json, does not verify that it is for the requested case, and does not verify that it records a passing result. A stale or attacker-created non-empty result.json can therefore make the smoke wrapper return success while no connector-level case evidence was produced. In CI or release workflows that use the smoke command exit status as a quality/security gate, this can create false PASS evidence and hide missing or failed runtime coverage.

title: Generated report freshness check preserves injected lines
description: Before this commit, `_write_known()` always rewrote generated report files with freshly generated content. The new `generated_report_equivalent()` helper strips every line whose prefix is `> Generated at: \`` from both the existing and candidate report, and `_write_known()` skips writing when the remaining lines match. Because the filter is not limited to a single trusted metadata header and does not validate the rest of the line, an attacker who can modify generated Markdown in a PR can add lines such as `> Generated at: `2026-01-01` ` anywhere in a generated report. Regeneration will consider the file equivalent and leave the attacker-supplied line intact. This undermines generated-report integrity checks and can lead to misleading published reports or Markdown/HTML injection in environments that render these reports.

title: Runtime path guard now allows unsafe /var paths
description: The path safety model previously rejected all /var and /var/* writes. This commit narrows that blocklist to only /var/lib, /var/run, and /var/log, adds /var/tmp/* as an allowed runtime root, and makes the default VERIFIED_RUN_ROOT a deterministic path under RUNNER_TEMP, TMPDIR, or /var/tmp. As a result, paths such as BUILD_ROOT=/var/www are accepted as safe because assert_safe_runtime_path first checks the user-supplied string against the weakened system-path list and then accepts anything equal to or under BUILD_ROOT. In addition, the default /var/tmp/ModSecurity-conector-verified path is predictable in a world-writable sticky directory; assert_safe_runtime_path does not canonicalize non-removal paths, so a pre-existing symlink at that location can bypass the source-checkout/system-root intent and cause subsequent mkdir/copy/build operations to write through the symlink. This can allow local build-root tampering, arbitrary artifact placement under unintended /var subtrees, or code execution in the context of a user/CI job that builds and executes generated sources from that runtime root.

title: Connector report freshness check bypassed
description: Previously, check-test-matrix depended on generate-test-matrix, so when a connector integration invoked it with CONNECTOR_ROOT/OUTPUT_ROOT pointing at the connector repository, the connector-owned reports under reports/testing were regenerated before git diff checked them. The commit changed the prerequisite to refresh-framework-reports, whose recipe forces CONNECTOR_ROOT and OUTPUT_ROOT to FRAMEWORK_ROOT. As a result, connector-specific reports are not regenerated, but the check still runs git diff against the caller's OUTPUT_ROOT. In connector CI, a malicious or stale reports/testing generated artifact can therefore remain undetected because the diff compares the working tree to itself rather than to freshly generated connector evidence. This weakens the report-integrity guard described by the framework threat model and can support false claims about connector security coverage.

title: Stale MRTS variant summaries can poison runtime reports
description: ci/run-runtime-matrix.sh runs the Apache and NGINX smokes with RESULTS_DIR forced to $BUILD_ROOT/results, so the fresh summaries for that run are written as $BUILD_ROOT/results/apache-summary.json and nginx-summary.json. However, update-runtime-snapshot.py now calls variant_summary_path(), which first looks for $BUILD_ROOT/results/$MODSECURITY_TEST_VARIANT/$MODSECURITY_MRTS_VARIANT/<connector>/<connector>-summary.json and uses it if it exists. Those variant directories are created by other MRTS targets via set_mrts_results_dir(). As a result, when a variant summary from a previous run, or one planted by a malicious connector/build step, exists, runtime-matrix can combine the current command exit code with stale per-case evidence from the variant path. Generated runtime matrices and coverage summaries may then report false per-case PASS results, undermining the integrity of security coverage reports.

title: Unconstrained MRTS paths allow destructive file writes
description: The commit adds MRTS generation/load helpers whose output locations are configurable through exported Make/environment variables. `ci/generate-mrts.sh` creates the selected rule/FTW output directories and then recursively removes `*.conf` and `*.yaml` files below them without checking that those paths are under `tests/mrts/generated` or another disposable build root. `ci/write-mrts-load.sh` similarly accepts `MRTS_LOAD_FILE`, writes a temporary file next to it, and renames it over the requested path. An attacker who can influence these environment variables or Make variables in a CI/build invocation could point them at sensitive writable locations, causing deletion of configuration/YAML files or overwrite/corruption of an arbitrary file. This bypasses the repository's existing pattern of constraining generated build paths and guarding destructive cleanup.

title: Non-promotable runtime evidence is reported as PASS
description: Runtime evidence that is explicitly marked non-promotable is now rendered and counted as ordinary PASS in generated coverage reports. The new normalizer maps any matrix status ending in `_PASS` or `_RESPONSE_BODY_PASS_THROUGH` to `PASS`, which erases the distinction used to prevent XFAIL, pending, future, connector-gap, runtime-difference, and RESPONSE_BODY pass-through evidence from becoming pass evidence. The committed runtime snapshot also contains RESPONSE_BODY rows with `matrix_status: PASS` while simultaneously setting `response_body_non_verified: true`, `runtime_verified: false`, and `promotion_allowed: false`. Generated HAProxy and runtime summary reports then include those rows in PASS counts and PASS details. This is a report-integrity/security-assurance issue: release or coverage decisions could incorrectly conclude that connector response-body or previously non-promotable security cases are verified.

title: RESPONSE_BODY strict aborts can be reported as PASS
description: The new response_body_pass_is_pass_through helper returns false for connection_aborted/aborted transport and for expected/actual statuses other than 200/200. That false value is then passed into matrix_status/semantic_matrix_status as if the case were not RESPONSE_BODY-related. For an active RESPONSE_BODY strict-abort or disruptive blocking case with raw status pass, the computed matrix status therefore becomes plain PASS. update-runtime-snapshot.py persists that value in matrix_status, and generate-case-matrix.py recomputes and overrides matrix_status for any RESPONSE_BODY raw pass row. Later non-promotion fields such as promotion_allowed=false do not prevent PASS status counts and matrix cells from being generated. This undermines the repository's explicit report-integrity invariant that RESPONSE_BODY runtime PASS must not render as plain PASS.

title: HAProxy reports trust PASS rows as verified coverage
description: The new HAProxy summary loader treats any nested HAProxy case whose status is "pass" as a verified runtime case, and treats any such row with requires_crs=true as CRS-verified. This is weaker than the removed synthetic HAProxy matrix path, which only promoted tightly scoped live evidence. A malformed, buggy, or malicious HAProxy smoke summary can therefore cause generated reports to claim HAProxy runtime verification and CRS verification for cases that were not actually live-executed or were not run with CRS loaded. The runtime matrix still has RESPONSE_BODY-specific non-promotion logic, but ordinary request-side blocking or CRS cases can be misrepresented in the new connector-smoke evidence path.

title: HAProxy prepare builds unverified cached source
description: ci/prepare-haproxy-runtime.sh downloads and verifies the official HAProxy tarball, but extract_source() returns immediately when HAPROXY_SOURCE_DIR already exists and REFRESH is not set. The later build step copies and runs make in that existing tree. Because Makefile recipes execute arbitrary shell commands, an attacker who can poison or persist files in the generated SOURCE_ROOT, for example through a shared CI cache, previous build artifact, or writable /src volume, can cause arbitrary code execution while the logs still show that the official archive checksum was verified. The same provenance weakness also appears for an existing HAPROXY_BIN, which is accepted as ready without tying it to the verified source. The helper should either fail on pre-existing source/binary paths unless an explicit trusted local-source mode is enabled, or remove and re-extract into a fresh canonicalized directory before building.

title: Traversal bypass in new smoke output root checks
description: The newly added smoke helpers intend to confine runtime artifacts to /src/ModSecurity-conector-build and its results/log/tmp subdirectories. However, the validators only match textual prefixes such as /src/* or $BUILD_ROOT/results/*. Paths containing '..' therefore pass validation but are resolved by the filesystem outside the intended directory. For example, with BUILD_ROOT=/src/ModSecurity-conector-build and RESULTS_DIR=/src/ModSecurity-conector-build/results/../../../../tmp/out, the new Envoy smoke runner accepts the path and writes envoy-results.jsonl, envoy-summary.json, and envoy-summary.txt under /tmp/out. The same pattern exists in the modified starter-check script, which can create/truncate results.jsonl, summary.json, and log files at escaped paths. This is not remotely exploitable by default, but in the framework's CI/build-chain threat model it weakens artifact-root containment when an attacker can influence smoke environment variables or Make invocation parameters.

title: With-CRS variant can falsely pass 401 status-action case
description: The changed YAML case is named action_status_401_phase1_block and its ModSecurity rule explicitly denies with status:401 and rule id 2320. The commit adds an expect.variants.with-crs override that changes only the expected HTTP status to 403. The new effective_expect() helper applies that override when MODSECURITY_TEST_VARIANT=with-crs, and assert_case_response() then only compares the observed response status against the effective status. Although rule_id remains present in the merged expectation, this assertion path does not verify that rule id 2320 actually fired. As a result, in With-CRS runs, a connector can return a generic CRS/default 403 or otherwise fail to honor the case's status:401 action and still satisfy the framework's PASS condition. This weakens runtime evidence for a security-relevant blocking/action test and can create false assurance in generated connector summaries.

title: CRS path validation permits out-of-root writes
description: The commit adds CRS support with environment-controlled CRS_SOURCE_DIR and CRS_RUNTIME_DIR. ci/fetch-crs.sh checks that CRS_SOURCE_DIR is absolute and lexically starts with SOURCE_ROOT, but it does not resolve the path or reject '..' components. A value such as CRS_SOURCE_DIR=$SOURCE_ROOT/../outside passes the check and causes git clone to create files outside SOURCE_ROOT. On clone failure, the same unchecked path is passed to rm -rf. ci/prepare-crs.sh only checks that CRS_SOURCE_DIR and CRS_RUNTIME_DIR are absolute, then creates directories and writes CRS setup/preamble files there, so CRS_RUNTIME_DIR can point outside BUILD_ROOT entirely. This defeats the framework's intended generated-root confinement for build/runtime artifacts.

title: ModSecurity v3 commit pin can be omitted from version check
description: The commit adds parsing for ModSecurity v3 approved literals and replaces the generic alias-based ModSecurity v3 release check with check_modsecurity_v3_release_provenance(). However, that new function only calls check_github_release_ref() with MODSECURITY_V3_APPROVED_REPO_URL and MODSECURITY_V3_RELEASE_TAG. MODSECURITY_V3_APPROVED_COMMIT is only added to result.variables for reporting; it is not checked for presence, non-emptiness, SHA-1 commit format, or consistency. Since validate_entries() only reports parsed entries that resolve empty, an entirely missing MODSECURITY_V3_APPROVED_COMMIT line is absent from entries and is not reported. A fixture containing the approved repo and release tag but omitting MODSECURITY_V3_APPROVED_COMMIT returns a successful ModSecurity v3 result when the fake latest release tag matches, validate_entries() returns [], and exit_code() returns 0. This violates the fail-closed provenance boundary for the immutable commit anchor.

title: Hash-chain validation ignores tampered volatile fields
description: The commit introduces an integrity hash-chain normalizer intended to detect evidence tampering. However, the canonical data used for compute_event_hash() is built with normalize_value(). That function replaces volatile-looking values such as timestamps, localhost ports, and paths containing ModSecurity/workspace with placeholders before hashing. As a result, two different raw evidence records can have the same canonical hash input. An attacker who can modify connector evidence can change those fields without causing validate_hash_chain() to report an event_hash mismatch. I verified this by hashing an event containing a timestamp and workspace path, changing both raw values, and observing that validate_hash_chain() still returned no errors.

title: Overbroad AGENTS.md include exemption bypasses doc checks
description: The new AGENTS.md include handling treats every root-level Markdown filename matched by an @Name.md line in AGENTS.md as local agent configuration. That exemption is then used by the repository path reference scanner and by the bilingual documentation partner check. Because the include name is not restricted to agent-specific files, a contributor can add, for example, @README.md to AGENTS.md and cause README.md to be skipped by the path-reference checker. The same exemption also causes README.md to bypass the required README.de.md partner check. This weakens CI documentation guardrails but does not expose code execution, credential disclosure, authentication bypass, or runtime security impact.

title: Security-data-flow cases break case discovery
description: The new files are placed under tests/cases/security-data-flow, which is part of the normal case discovery tree. However, runner_core.load_case() validates every discovered or explicitly selected case before applicability filtering. The new cases omit the required rules field, declare a new security_data_flow capability that is not in KNOWN_CAPABILITIES, and several also omit the required expect.status integer. As a result, workflows or connector harnesses that list/select/materialize these cases fail with ValueError instead of treating them as pending connector-gap inventory. I confirmed this by running case_cli.py list-cases with --test-case tests/cases/security-data-flow/headers/header_count_limit_exceeded.yaml, which fails with 'case requires rules'.
